stable_user_preferences: Use plain Chinese explanations and concrete steps.
Do not rush into implementation before confirming product direction.
The user wants to manage the game, not manually manage Agents or Sessions.
Preserve the existing AGENTS.md, docs, memory-bank, state and prompt management approach.
Prefer evidence-backed claims; mark unknown and unverified facts explicitly.
Review each implementation phase through a pushed GitHub commit before allowing the next phase.
Keep the repository public and sanitize any host/user paths in published evidence.
All model-dependent verification must use the real commandcode provider; never substitute another provider to make a test pass.
confirmed_product_decisions: AI Game Studio is an AI game R&D advisor and automation platform.
DSH is the single AI runtime; Studio owns deterministic business workflows and controls.
Support idea discussion, formal R&D and change request workspaces separately.
Global shared asset library plus project-specific asset library.
Support project import and global Inbox import.
Analyze change impact and obtain approval before updating the baseline.
Exclude post-release monitoring, operation analytics, post-release advisor and iteration.
verified_technical_facts: The user runs DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3 (bundled runtime) with provider commandcode (@mars-sea/dsh-commandcode-provider@0.15.4) and model deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash. The dsh CLI on PATH is 0.1.5-rc.1 and is NOT what the user actually runs.

The commandcode plugin declares dsh compatibility >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.2.2-0, so it cannot be used on 0.1.5; an incompatible plugin is skipped silently and the runtime falls back to another provider (observed: deepseek-official -> HTTP 402).
Every probe must assert request/header.config.provider and .model, otherwise a provider fallback is mistaken for a model failure.
DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 SDK protocol methods: initialize, session/prompt, session/resume, session/wait, session/working-directory/get|set, shutdown. No cancel, no approve, no session/close.
session/resume on 0.2.1 restores conversation history across a full process restart (verified by token recall); 0.1.5 has no resume and rejects sessionId reuse with already exists.
MCP is the only tool-registration path; on 0.2.1 the model really invoked mcp__studio__get_studio_health and the Studio server recorded tools/call + tools/call.served.
Process reclamation must be three-state (PRESENT/ABSENT/CHECK_FAILED); a failed query is never evidence of absence. Orphan matching needs command-line markers, not just the parent-child chain.
A process check must exclude its own enumeration process (unique sentinel) and conhost.exe, or it observes itself and reports a phantom leftover.
dsh-atomic-write never checks whether the lock-holder pid is alive; a dead-pid profiles/node_modules.lock makes the next boot fail after a 2000 ms deadline, surfaced only as JSON-RPC input closed.
Startup time is bimodal: 2-3 s warm vs 73-128 s when profiles/node_modules must be rebuilt (187 entries, 164 symlinks); the SDK default initializeTimeoutMs of 10 s is unusable.
This host injects a safe-delete shim via NODE_OPTIONS that can abort DSH profile maintenance with SAFE_DELETE_BULK_CONFIRM_REQUIRED; that is environment interference, not a runtime defect.

Patch files use two shapes: insert: for new rows, a bare id: row to override an existing row. Inserting llm-commandcode alone does not change the default model; agent-default-model must be overridden too.

A redaction gate must be falsifiable: the first two versions of scrub-evidence.mjs reported "0 residual" because the Windows pattern required two backslashes while decoded paths have one, and because only four directories were scanned. It now scans git-tracked files (152), parses JSON first, and is validated by planting a leak and confirming exit 1.

Scripted string replacement can silently comment out code: a literal //n (an un-escaped newline) made // swallow the first route assertion in CC-3 and CC-4, so only the second run/turn was checked while the report claimed both were. Read back and assert on actual values after any scripted edit.

fs.cpSync and bulk fs.rmSync terminate this node process with exit 127 and no message under the host safe-delete shim; manual recursive copy works and npm ci is unaffected. Setup therefore never deletes a tree.

A dependency fingerprint is not a lockfile. profile-locks/<profile>/package-lock.json is a real npm lockfile used by npm ci; a version that disagrees with it raises DependencyDriftError and aborts the run.
CC-0 is a CLI probe and emits no request/header event, so it cannot prove which provider served the request. Only CC-1..CC-4 carry route assertions.
Each probe run so far observed exactly one request/header per turn, including the tool-using CC-2, so multi-hop (tool call then second request) route coverage is still unobserved.

Redaction and leak detection must share one rule set. They were written twice with different patterns, which is why the gate reported clean while evidence kept leaking; src/lib/redact.mjs is now the only definition.
A gate must be proven falsifiable. Tests plant a path, corrupt a lock, delete a lock, break an installed file, and assert the exit code or returned value — never a log line.
The suite runs the leak scan itself (src/lib/scrub.mjs) after the probes and folds it into the verdict. Six passing probes do not outvote a leaked path: overall FAIL, exit 1.

Dependency verification needs the installed bytes, not just the version string: profile-locks/<profile>/tree.json stores file count and sha256, and a mismatch triggers a deterministic reinstall from the lockfile.
A normal run never generates a lockfile. Missing lock is a hard failure (lock-missing); regeneration is a separate maintenance command (npm run lock:update).
CC-0 classifies failures from stdout AND stderr (src/lib/diagnostics.mjs); the model writes its reasoning to stderr, so keeping a stderr tail is a privacy leak, not just noise.
Route assertions now live in src/lib/assertions.mjs and are unit-tested with an empty list, a wrong model and a second-hop fallback, so the vacuous-true case cannot return unnoticed.
Every probe run so far observed exactly one request/header per turn, including the tool-using CC-2; multi-hop coverage remains unobserved and is recorded as such in routeShape.

A report must never embed its own commit SHA. Backfilling the SHA changed the report, so the fixed commit the reviewer opened was not the delivered version. SHA now lives only in state/project_state.json, written by a metadata-only commit that does not touch the report.
Do not use an extension whitelist for a leak scan: .gitignore and package.json.orig were skipped that way. Scan every published file; skip binary by NUL byte and report skippedBinary.

A path segment class that rejects all whitespace misses ordinary directories with spaces. Allow spaces but keep the regex linear; nested star quantifiers cause catastrophic backtracking and heap exhaustion.
findLeaks must build its RegExp with the g flag. Without it exec restarts at index 0 forever and an infinite loop exhausts the heap.
Credential-shaped values need their own redaction rules and tests, even when no real key has leaked yet; otherwise the code cannot prove it protects credentials.
Dependency integrity requires comparing tree.json integrity AND resolved against package-lock.json, not merely checking that the fields exist. Staging cache reuse must not bypass that comparison.
A failing test run must not overwrite published evidence. Use an explicit output path and publish only on a real zero exit code; prove it with fault injection.

A project state file may have exactly one current record. This repository once had three documents each declaring a different object as the only authority, and two historical objects still said the real-prompt and MCP-tool gates were BLOCKED while the report said PASS. state.phase_00_final plus authoritative_source.current_record now define the single source.

State consistency must be an executable pre-flight gate, not a documentation promise. checkProjectState() in src/lib/gates.mjs runs before any probe in run-all.mjs and as a third gate in scripts/run-gates.mjs; a broken state aborts with exit 1 and zero model calls.

Historical state objects are read-only evidence. Never delete them to make the current status look clean; label them historical and keep them. The gate explicitly fails if a historical round record disappears.

A DEFERRED item needs a target phase, a risk, and a verification condition; an UNKNOWN item needs why_unknown and condition_to_verify. UNKNOWN is not PASS, BLOCKED is not FAIL, NOT_SUPPORTED is not "not observed".

WorkBuddy being able to use HY4 on a free tier only proves the IDE side works. It does not prove DSH can call HY4 through an official interface, and PHASE 00 DeepSeek probes are not HY4 compatibility evidence. Record as an independent UNKNOWN, never as CONFIRMED or blocking.
A child process raw stderr can bypass the redacted output layer when it contains an uncaught exception stack trace. Even wrappers that forward child output must go through src/lib/safe-output.mjs.

A PHASE 00 gate set is defined in phases/PHASE_00_FEASIBILITY_DSH_VERTICAL_SLICE.md. Items outside those ten gates are not automatically blockers; decide by scope, core-chain impact, verified alternatives and risk, then record DEFERRED with a target phase.
do_not_assume: Electron is not approved yet; ADR-0001 is PROPOSED / CONDITIONAL pending packaged smoke tests.
Local database choice is still deferred to PHASE 01.
Never upgrade the user global DSH or change ~/.dsh profiles; verify against an isolated DSH_HOME.
Repository visibility is public by explicit user instruction; do not change it.
Do not claim a dependable tool-approval callback exists in 0.1.5 or 0.2.1: it is UNKNOWN / NOT_OBSERVED. Only the session/approve method is NOT_SUPPORTED.
Do not cite CC-0 as provider-route evidence; it has no request/header.
Do not treat "no approval callback observed" as "no approval callback exists" — it is UNKNOWN/NOT_OBSERVED.
Do not run fs.cpSync or bulk fs.rmSync against dsh-home or node_modules on this host; the shim kills the process.
Do not add a second redaction implementation; extend src/lib/redact.mjs.
Do not write to stdout/stderr directly in probe code; use src/lib/safe-output.mjs.
Do not let a run auto-create a lockfile and then claim reproducibility.
Do not put the delivery commit SHA into the delivery report.
Do not re-run the six real model probes for a change that only touches redaction, scanning, dependency metadata or docs.
Do not cite phase_00.gate_results, phase_00_r1.gate_results or any r11..r141 object as current state; use state.phase_00_final.
Do not re-run the six real model probes for a change that touches only state, docs or gate orchestration; label the retained evidence as such instead of claiming a new test.
Do not invent a DSH/HY4 compatibility result, require a paid API key, or use WorkBuddy private interfaces as a product dependency.
Do not open another PHASE 00 remediation round after this finalisation; the remaining items belong to PHASE 01 or to a user decision.
